shuttle.description: Hikasus Travel offers private transfers from any city of Georgia, providing safe and convenient transportation in sedans, minivans, minibuses, and larger vehicles. Whether you're traveling from Tbilisi to Batumi, Yerevan (Armenia), Kutaisi, Kazbegi, or any other destination – or simply return – our professional drivers ensure a smooth and hassle-free journey. Ideal for solo travelers, families, and groups, our transfer services are comfortable, punctual, and competitively priced. Book your transfer today and explore Georgia with ease!

benefits.plannedText: From airport pickup to every hotel, meal, and activity — your entire trip is organized down to the last detail before you arrive.

blog.article3.desc: Georgia is not named after St George — that's a medieval mistake that stuck. The real story runs through Persian, and Georgians call it Sakartvelo.
blog.article4.title: The Georgian Flag: Five Crosses, Eight Centuries, and One Revolution
blog.article4.desc: Georgia's five-cross flag looks medieval and is — but it only became the national flag in 2004, carried first as a protest banner. The real story is stranger than the legend.

ptc.tours-from-tbilisi.title: Private Tours from Tbilisi, Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.tours-from-tbilisi.description: Private tours starting in Tbilisi, from a three-day Kakheti wine trip to a twenty-day grand tour. Your driver-guide meets you at the airport or your hotel.
ptc.tours-from-tbilisi.intro: Most of our trips begin in Tbilisi, which makes sense: it is where nearly everyone lands, and the Georgian Military Highway, the Kakheti wine country and the road west all start from here. The tours below are the ones whose first day is a Tbilisi day — your driver-guide meets you at the airport or your hotel, and you set off from the capital. They range from a three-day run into Kakheti to a twenty-day loop taking in the Caucasus, Svaneti and the Black Sea coast, with a winter option up to Gudauri. Every one is private, so the pace, the stops and the hotel standard are yours to set.
ptc.tours-from-kutaisi.title: Private Tours from Kutaisi, Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.tours-from-kutaisi.description: Private tours starting in Kutaisi, useful if you fly into Kutaisi International rather than Tbilisi. Seven to thirteen days across western Georgia and the Caucasus.
ptc.tours-from-kutaisi.intro: Kutaisi has its own international airport, and for a lot of travellers on low-cost European routes it is the cheaper way into Georgia. These tours are built to start there rather than making you transfer four hours to Tbilisi first. From Kutaisi you are already among the things people come west for — Gelati and Motsameta, the Prometheus Cave, the canyons at Martvili and Okatse — and the road north into Svaneti is shorter. The trips below run from seven to thirteen days, working east towards Tbilisi and the Caucasus, or north into the mountains. All are private, with transport and accommodation arranged according to the individual itinerary.
ptc.cultural-heritage-tours.h1: Cultural and Heritage Tours in Georgia
ptc.cultural-heritage-tours.title: Cultural & Heritage Tours in Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.cultural-heritage-tours.description: Tours built around Georgia’s monasteries, cave towns and old capitals — Mtskheta, Uplistsikhe, Gelati, David Gareja — from three days to two weeks.
ptc.cultural-heritage-tours.intro: Georgia has been Christian since the fourth century and inhabited far longer, and the buildings show it: cathedrals that predate most of Europe’s, monasteries cut into bare rock, and whole towns carved out of hillsides. These tours are the ones weighted towards that history. Between them they cover Mtskheta and Svetitskhoveli, the hilltop Jvari monastery, the cave town at Uplistsikhe, Gelati and Motsameta near Kutaisi, and the desert monastery at David Gareja near the Azerbaijani border. Most pair the sites with the everyday side of the country — a market, a family winery, a long lunch — because that is usually what people remember. Lengths run from three days to two weeks.
ptc.wine-food-tours.h1: Wine and Food Tours in Georgia
ptc.wine-food-tours.title: Wine & Food Tours in Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.wine-food-tours.description: Qvevri winemaking, family cellars in Kakheti and Georgian cooking, on trips from three days to three weeks. Tastings at Tsinandali, Khareba, Shumi and small local wineries.
ptc.wine-food-tours.intro: Georgians have been fermenting wine in buried clay qvevri for about eight thousand years, and it is still how a lot of the country makes it — including plenty of families who press a few hundred litres for themselves each autumn. These trips put that front and centre. Depending on the tour you taste at big estates like Tsinandali and Khareba and at small cellars where the owner pours, get hands-on with a qvevri, and eat your way through the regional cooking that goes with it. Kakheti in the east is the heart of it, though the longer tours pick up Adjarian and Imeretian food on the way. Three days to three weeks.
ptc.adventure-hiking-tours.h1: Adventure and Hiking Tours in Georgia
ptc.adventure-hiking-tours.title: Adventure & Hiking Tours in Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.adventure-hiking-tours.description: Walking in the Georgian Caucasus — Juta and the Chaukhi peaks, Truso valley, Gergeti and Svaneti — on trips of eight to twenty days, plus three winter ski trips.
ptc.adventure-hiking-tours.intro: The Caucasus is high, close to the road, and much emptier than the Alps, which is what makes walking here worth the trip. These tours build in real days on foot rather than a token stroll: the trek up the Juta valley under the Chaukhi peaks, the glacial Truso valley with its mineral springs and abandoned hamlets, the climb to Gergeti Trinity at 2,170 metres, and the rough tracks of Svaneti. Nothing here needs technical skill, but you should be comfortable walking four or five hours. The trips run from eight to twenty days, and three are winter ski itineraries: a focused Gudauri week from Tbilisi, an 8-day Gudauri stay from Kutaisi, and a longer Gudauri–Bakuriani combination from Kutaisi.
ptc.nature-mountain-tours.h1: Nature and Mountain Tours in Georgia
ptc.nature-mountain-tours.title: Nature & Mountain Tours in Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.nature-mountain-tours.description: The Georgian Caucasus, Svaneti’s tower villages, the Martvili and Okatse canyons and the Prometheus Cave, on private trips of seven to twenty days.
ptc.nature-mountain-tours.intro: Georgia is a small country that goes from subtropical coast to five-thousand-metre peaks in a few hours’ drive, and these are the tours that lean into the landscape. Between them they cover the Georgian Military Highway up to Kazbegi under Mount Kazbek, the tower villages of Svaneti below Shkhara, the green-water canyons at Martvili and Okatse, and the lit chambers of the Prometheus Cave. Some days are spent walking, others are simply long scenic drives with the right stops built in. Lengths run from a week to twenty days, and because every trip is private you can slow a mountain day down when the weather is good.
ptc.black-sea-tours.title: Black Sea Tours in Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.black-sea-tours.description: Tours that reach the coast at Batumi — the botanical garden, the boulevard and Adjarian cooking — combined with the Caucasus and the wine country. Five to twenty days.
ptc.black-sea-tours.intro: Batumi is the odd one out in Georgia: subtropical, loud, half glass towers and half nineteenth-century facades, with palm trees along the seafront and the Turkish border half an hour away. These are the tours that actually reach the coast and spend nights there, rather than passing through western Georgia on the way somewhere else. On the coast you get the hillside botanical garden north of town, the boulevard and the Argo cable car, the moving Ali and Nino statue, and Adjarian cooking — above all the boat-shaped khachapuri with an egg on top. Each trip pairs the sea with the mountains or the wine country inland. Five to twenty days.
ptc.winter-tours.title: Winter Tours in Georgia | Hikasus Travel
ptc.winter-tours.description: Three private ski trips in Georgia — Gudauri weeks from Tbilisi and from Kutaisi, and an eleven-day Gudauri and Bakuriani journey, with transfers, hotels and flexible ski days arranged.
ptc.winter-tours.intro: Georgia’s ski season runs roughly from December to early April, with Gudauri high on the Caucasus ridge and Bakuriani offering a lower, forested alternative. Gudauri is known for broad above-the-tree-line pistes and open freeride terrain, while Bakuriani offers gentler, more sheltered skiing. Our private winter tours now include Gudauri ski stays from both Tbilisi and Kutaisi, as well as a longer two-resort journey combining Gudauri and Bakuriani. Hotels and transfers are arranged, while the ski days stay flexible so you can spend your mountain time at your own pace.
